# gitmoap_group_catalog_deployments (Data Source)

The deployment board — services × environments. Lists the group's services, alphabetically, each with its current deployment in every environment the group can deploy to, its own and those inherited from groups above it. Environments owned by a group you cannot see are left out. Every other environment is a column on every page, up to 500; a board that would show more is refused, so narrow the environments with `environment_id` or `tier`. Narrow the services with `search`; pages hold up to 100 services (20 by default). Commits-behind counts are not included here; ask the drift endpoint for them.

The token needs `catalog:read`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "gitmoap_group_by_path" "acme" {
  full_path = "acme"
}

data "gitmoap_group_catalog_deployments" "acme" {
  group_id = data.gitmoap_group_by_path.acme.group_id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `group_id` (String) The group whose services the board lists

### Optional

- `environment_id` (String) Show only these environments, as a comma-separated list of ids
- `search` (String) Match a service's name, description or slug substring
- `tier` (String) Show only environments of this tier

### Read-Only

- `environments` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--environments))
- `rows` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rows))

<a id="nestedatt--environments"></a>
### Nested Schema for `environments`

Read-Only:

- `archived` (Boolean)
- `display_name` (String)
- `environment_id` (String)
- `scope` (Attributes) A group or a repository, whichever a setting belongs to.

Set one of `group` or `repo`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--environments--scope))
- `slug` (String)
- `tier` (String) What kind of environment this is, whatever it is called: `development`, `testing`, `staging`
or `production`. A `production` environment is protected by default.
- `url` (String)

<a id="nestedatt--environments--scope"></a>
### Nested Schema for `environments.scope`

Read-Only:

- `group` (String)
- `repo` (String)



<a id="nestedatt--rows"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rows`

Read-Only:

- `cells` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rows--cells))
- `service` (Attributes) The short form of a service that listings, search results and path lookups show. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rows--service))

<a id="nestedatt--rows--cells"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rows.cells`

Read-Only:

- `commits_behind` (Number) How many commits the deployment is behind its repository's default branch. Only present
when the request asks for it.
- `deployment` (Attributes) A deployment in brief, as the deployment board, a service's overview and its history show it. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rows--cells--deployment))
- `environment_id` (String)

<a id="nestedatt--rows--cells--deployment"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rows.cells.deployment`

Read-Only:

- `commit_sha` (String)
- `deployed_at` (String)
- `deployment_id` (String)
- `environment_id` (String)
- `pipeline_run_id` (String)
- `repository_id` (String)
- `service_id` (String)
- `status` (String) Where a deployment is in its life. It starts `requested`; waits as `awaiting_approval` when the
environment needs approval, ending `rejected` if refused; then `running`, ending `succeeded`,
`failed` or `cancelled`. `skipped` means another deploy held the environment and its policy is to
skip. A successful deployment becomes `superseded` when a later one replaces it.



<a id="nestedatt--rows--service"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rows.service`

Read-Only:

- `display_name` (String)
- `external` (Boolean)
- `group_id` (String)
- `kind` (String) What sort of thing a service is. The kind decides which scorecard checks apply: a `library` has
no deployments, so a deployment check is not applicable to it rather than failing. For your own
classifications, use annotations.
- `lifecycle` (String) Where a service is in its life.
- `orphaned_at` (String)
- `owner` (Attributes) Who owns a service: a group, a team, or a person or service account. A service may also have no
owner, which the `has_owner` scorecard check surfaces.

`kind` says which applies: `group`, with `full_path`, `group_id`; `principal`, with `actor`, `principal_id`; `team`, with `organization`, `slug`, `team_id`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rows--service--owner))
- `service_id` (String)
- `slug` (String)
- `source` (String) How the catalog entry came to exist. Set by the platform, never accepted from a request. Any
source other than `inferred` means a person has vouched for the entry.

<a id="nestedatt--rows--service--owner"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rows.service.owner`

Read-Only:

- `actor` (Attributes) Who did something — a person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — with what a
client needs to draw and link them, so a page of records names its actors without a lookup each. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rows--service--owner--actor))
- `full_path` (String)
- `group_id` (String)
- `kind` (String)
- `organization` (String) The full path of the organization's top-level group, such as `acme`.
- `principal_id` (String)
- `slug` (String) The team's slug, such as `backend`.
- `team_id` (String)

<a id="nestedatt--rows--service--owner--actor"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rows.service.owner.actor`

Read-Only:

- `avatar_url` (String) The principal's picture, when one is known. Absent otherwise: a client derives the
deterministic avatar URL itself.
- `email` (String) The principal's address. An agent's is a generated no-reply address — the author of its
commits. `unknown` on a deleted actor and empty on a redacted one.
- `id` (String) The principal's id: a user id, a service account id or an agent id, as `kind` says. Empty on
a redacted actor.
- `kind` (String) A person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — which of the three a principal is,
and so which page it links to: a person's profile, a service account's page or an agent's page.
- `username` (String) The name to show: a person's or service account's username, or an agent's handle (which
always ends in `-ai`). `deleted-user` when the actor no longer resolves, `redacted` when the
caller may not see who it was. A closed account whose work stays is `closed-` and twelve hex
digits, a shape no open account may take, with an address under `.invalid`.
